category: Ports & subsystems, user-defined functions & model verification blocks (extended)
description: Control ports, iterator and event-function blocks of the Ports & Subsystems library, variant and state/parameter access blocks of Signal Routing, the remaining User-Defined Functions blocks (S-functions, Fcn, C Function) and the complete Model Verification library of run-time assertion blocks.

tools.name: Enable
tools.description: Adds an enable port to a subsystem or referenced model so that it executes only while the enable signal is greater than zero. Dropping it into any Subsystem turns it into an enabled subsystem; its parameters decide whether states are held or reset when the subsystem is re-enabled.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Enable  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Enable', [subsys '/Enable'])

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling
parameters.description: 'held' (default) keeps states from the previous activation; 'reset' returns them to their initial conditions.

parameters.name: ShowOutputPort
parameters.description: 'on' adds an output port inside the subsystem that carries the enable signal value.

parameters.name: ZeroCross
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off'. Zero-crossing detection on the enable signal for variable-step solvers.

parameters.name: PropagateVarSize
parameters.description: 'Only when enabling' or 'During execution' - when variable-size signal dimensions may change.

tools.notes: Only one Enable block is allowed per subsystem. Combine with a Trigger block to create an enabled and triggered subsystem. In a referenced model the Enable block goes at the root level of the referenced model.

tools.name: Trigger
tools.description: Adds a trigger or function-call port to a subsystem or referenced model. With an edge trigger type the subsystem executes once per rising, falling or either edge of the control signal; with 'function-call' it runs whenever a function-call initiator (Stateflow chart, Function-Call Generator, S-function) calls it.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Trigger  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Trigger', [subsys '/Trigger'])

parameters.name: TriggerType
parameters.description: 'rising' | 'falling' | 'either' | 'function-call' | 'message'.

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling
parameters.description: For function-call triggers: 'held', 'reset' or 'inherit' - state handling when the subsystem is re-enabled.

parameters.name: ShowOutputPort
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the trigger signal (or the edge direction) inside the subsystem.

parameters.name: SampleTimeType
parameters.description: For function-call triggers: 'triggered' or 'periodic' (lets the subsystem declare a rate for export-function models).

parameters.name: InitialTriggerSignalState
parameters.description: How the first sample of the trigger signal is interpreted: 'zero', 'positive', 'negative' or compatibility mode.

tools.notes: Blocks inside an edge-triggered subsystem must have inherited (-1) sample time. Export-function models use root-level Inport blocks with 'Output function call' instead of Trigger blocks for each function.

tools.name: Action Port
tools.description: The control port of If Action and Switch Case Action subsystems. It connects the subsystem to an output of an If or Switch Case block so that the subsystem executes only when that branch is selected, like the body of an if/elseif/else or case statement.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Action Port (found inside If Action Subsystem / Switch Case Action Subsystem)

parameters.name: InitializeStates
parameters.description: 'held' (default) or 'reset' - whether states are reset when the action subsystem becomes active again.

parameters.name: PropagateVarSize
parameters.description: When variable-size signal dimensions are propagated: 'Only when execution is resumed' or 'During execution'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/If Action Subsystem', [mdl '/ThenBranch']);
set_param([mdl '/ThenBranch/Action Port'], 'InitializeStates', 'reset');
tools.notes: Outputs of mutually exclusive action subsystems are normally combined with a Merge block; set OutputWhenDisabled on the Out1 blocks to 'held' in that pattern.

tools.name: Function-Call Generator
tools.description: Emits function-call events at a fixed sample time to execute function-call subsystems or function-call models periodically, optionally several times per step. Useful for testing export-function models and for building explicit schedulers.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Function-Call Generator  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Generator', [mdl '/FCG'])

parameters.name: sample_time
parameters.description: Rate at which function-call events are generated (default '1').

parameters.name: numberOfIterations
parameters.description: Number of function calls issued per time step (default '1'); a vector produces a wide function-call signal.

parameters.name: ShowEnablePort
parameters.description: 'on' adds an enable input that gates the calls.

parameters.name: DisallowWideOutput
parameters.description: 'on' forbids a wide (vector) function-call output.

tools.notes: Since R2025a it is a built-in block (BlockType 'FunctionCallGenerator') rather than a masked library link. Use a Function-Call Split to drive several subsystems from one generator.

tools.name: Function-Call Split
tools.description: Branches one function-call line so that it can call several function-call subsystems or models in a deterministic order. The subsystem connected to the output port marked with a dot executes first.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Function-Call Split  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Split', [mdl '/Split'])

parameters.name: NumOutputPorts
parameters.description: Number of function-call branches (default '2').

parameters.name: OutputPortLayout
parameters.description: 'default' or 'reverse' ordering of the output ports.

parameters.name: IconShape
parameters.description: 'distinctive' (default) or 'round'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Split', [mdl '/Split']);
set_param([mdl '/Split'], 'NumOutputPorts', '3');
tools.notes: Plain line branching of function-call signals is not allowed; always use this block. View the resulting order with Debug > Information Overlays > Execution Order. Data dependencies between the branches may require a Function-Call Feedback Latch.

tools.name: Function-Call Feedback Latch
tools.description: Breaks a data feedback loop between function-call subsystems that are called by the same initiator or by a parent-child pair. It latches the value so the reader sees the value from the previous call, resolving the data-dependency error without adding a Unit Delay's sample-time semantics.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Function-Call Feedback Latch  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Function-Call Feedback Latch', [mdl '/Latch'])
tools.notes: Equivalent to selecting 'Latch input for feedback signals of function-call subsystem outputs' on the Inport block inside the reading subsystem. Supports numeric, fixed-point, enumerated and bus signals.

tools.name: For Iterator
tools.description: Control block placed inside a subsystem to repeat the subsystem's execution a fixed or externally supplied number of times within a single time step, the block-diagram equivalent of a for loop. It optionally outputs the iteration index.
tools.usage: Inside a For Iterator Subsystem (Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > For Iterator Subsystem) or added to any subsystem

parameters.name: IterationSource
parameters.description: 'internal' uses IterationLimit; 'external' adds an input port for the limit.

parameters.name: IterationLimit
parameters.description: Number of iterations (default '5').

parameters.name: ResetStates
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' - state handling at the start of each time step.

parameters.name: ExternalIncrement
parameters.description: 'on' adds a Next i input to set the next index from inside the loop.

parameters.name: ShowIterationPort
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the iteration variable.

parameters.name: IndexMode
parameters.description: 'One-based' or 'Zero-based'.

parameters.name: IterationVariableDataType
parameters.description: 'int32' (default), 'uint32', 'int16', 'uint16', 'int8', 'uint8' or 'double'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/For Iterator Subsystem', [mdl '/Loop']);
set_param([mdl '/Loop/For Iterator'], 'IterationLimit', '10', 'IndexMode', 'Zero-based');
tools.notes: Blocks inside the loop need inherited or constant sample times. Use an Assignment block with a Memory or Unit Delay feedback to build an array element by element across iterations.

tools.name: While Iterator
tools.description: Control block that repeats its subsystem within one time step while a condition input is true, implementing while or do-while loops. An optional iteration-number output and a maximum iteration count protect against infinite loops.
tools.usage: Inside a While Iterator Subsystem (Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > While Iterator Subsystem)

parameters.name: MaxIters
parameters.description: Maximum iterations per time step (default '5'); -1 means unlimited.

parameters.name: WhileBlockType
parameters.description: 'while' (checks an external IC input first) or 'do-while' (runs once before checking the condition).

parameters.name: ResetStates
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset'.

parameters.name: ShowIterationPort
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the current iteration number.

parameters.name: OutputDataType
parameters.description: Data type of the iteration number output, default 'int32'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/While Iterator Subsystem', [mdl '/Solve']);
set_param([mdl '/Solve/While Iterator'], 'WhileBlockType', 'do-while', 'MaxIters', '100', 'ShowIterationPort', 'on');
tools.notes: With MaxIters = -1 a condition that never becomes false hangs the simulation; press Ctrl+C in MATLAB to abort.

tools.name: For Each
tools.description: Control block inside a For Each Subsystem that partitions input signals (and optionally mask parameters) into slices, executes the subsystem once per slice with separate states for each, and concatenates the outputs. Ideal for vectorising a scalar algorithm over many channels.
tools.usage: Inside a For Each Subsystem (Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > For Each Subsystem)

parameters.name: InputPartition
parameters.description: Per input port: whether it is partitioned ('on') or passed whole.

parameters.name: InputPartitionDimension / InputPartitionWidth / InputPartitionOffset
parameters.description: Dimension to slice along, slice width and gap/overlap between slices.

parameters.name: SubsysMaskParameterPartition
parameters.description: Partition mask parameters of the parent subsystem so each iteration gets its own parameter slice.

parameters.name: OutputConcatenationDimension
parameters.description: Dimension along which per-iteration outputs are stacked.

parameters.name: ShowIterationIndex
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the current partition index.

parameters.name: SpecifiedNumIters
parameters.description: Number of partitions to process; -1 (default) processes all.

tools.notes: Each iteration keeps independent states, unlike For Iterator. Code generation produces a loop over a state array, reusing one function body.

tools.name: Enabled and Triggered Subsystem
tools.description: Preconfigured subsystem containing both an Enable and a Trigger port. It executes once on each trigger event but only if the enable signal is positive at that moment, for example sampling a sensor on a clock edge only while a system is armed.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Enabled and Triggered Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Enabled and Triggered Subsystem', [mdl '/ET'])

parameters.name: TriggerType (Trigger block)
parameters.description: 'rising', 'falling' or 'either' edge of the trigger input.

parameters.name: StatesWhenEnabling (Enable block)
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' when re-enabled.

parameters.name: OutputWhenDisabled (Out1 blocks)
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' output while not executing.

tools.notes: Contents must use inherited sample times, as in any triggered subsystem.

tools.name: Switch Case Action Subsystem
tools.description: Subsystem with an Action Port that executes when the connected case of a Switch Case block is selected. Together with Switch Case and Merge it implements C-style switch statements in a block diagram, with each case generating a separate code branch.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Switch Case Action Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Switch Case Action Subsystem', [mdl '/Case1'])

parameters.name: InitializeStates (Action Port)
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' when the case becomes active again.

tools.notes: Blocks inside must use inherited or constant sample times. Connect every action subsystem output to a Merge block to form a single signal.

tools.name: Atomic Subsystem
tools.description: A Subsystem block with 'Treat as atomic unit' already selected, so its contents execute as a single unit in the sorted order and it can be generated as its own function. Use it to control execution grouping, set a subsystem-level sample time, or apply Function Packaging for code generation.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Atomic Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Atomic Subsystem', [mdl '/Algo'])

parameters.name: TreatAsAtomicUnit
parameters.description: 'on' for an atomic (nonvirtual) subsystem.

parameters.name: RTWSystemCode
parameters.description: Function packaging: 'Auto', 'Inline', 'Nonreusable function' or 'Reusable function'.

parameters.name: SystemSampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time for the whole subsystem, -1 to inherit.

parameters.name: MinAlgLoopOccurrences
parameters.description: 'on' tries to eliminate artificial algebraic loops involving the subsystem.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Atomic Subsystem', [mdl '/Algo']);
set_param([mdl '/Algo'], 'RTWSystemCode', 'Reusable function', 'RTWFcnNameOpts', 'User specified', 'RTWFcnName', 'algo_step');
tools.notes: Atomic subsystems can introduce algebraic loops that would not exist with a virtual subsystem. The CodeReuse Subsystem library block is an atomic subsystem preset for reusable functions.

tools.name: Initialize Function
tools.description: Preconfigured subsystem that executes once on the model initialize event, before the first time step. Inside it, State Writer, Parameter Writer and Data Store Write blocks set initial states, parameters or data from computed values rather than fixed initial-condition parameters.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Initialize Function  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Initialize Function', [mdl '/Init'])

parameters.name: EventType (Event Listener)
parameters.description: 'Initialize' for this block; the same subsystem template is reused with 'Reinitialize', 'Reset' or 'Terminate'.

tools.notes: In an export-function or component model the initialize event becomes an entry-point function in generated code. Only one Initialize Function per model hierarchy level is recommended; see also Reinitialize, Reset and Terminate Function.

tools.name: Reinitialize Function
tools.description: Subsystem that executes when a named reinitialize event is raised, typically to reinitialize block states partway through a simulation (for example after a mode change) without restarting. In referenced models it appears as a reinitialize port on the Model block.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Reinitialize Function  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Reinitialize Function', [mdl '/Reinit'])

parameters.name: EventName (Event Listener)
parameters.description: Name of the reinitialize event, default 'reinit'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Reinitialize Function', [mdl '/Reinit']);
set_param([mdl '/Reinit/Event Listener'], 'EventName', 'reinitAfterFault');
tools.notes: Reinitialize replaced the earlier use of Reset Function for this purpose; use Reset Function when the generated code needs a reset entry point.

tools.name: Reset Function
tools.description: Subsystem executed when a named reset event occurs. In a component model it generates a separate reset() entry-point function that the calling application invokes, and in simulation it is triggered through the reset port of the referencing Model block.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Reset Function  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Reset Function', [mdl '/Reset'])

parameters.name: EventName (Event Listener)
parameters.description: Name of the reset event, default 'reset'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Reset Function', [mdl '/Reset']);
% inside: State Writer blocks re-load integrator states from Constant blocks
tools.notes: Only valid at the root of a model; nested usage inside other subsystems is not supported.

tools.name: Terminate Function
tools.description: Subsystem that executes once on the model terminate event at the end of simulation. Use State Reader, Data Store Write or To Workspace style logic inside it to save final states to nonvolatile memory or perform cleanup.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Terminate Function  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Terminate Function', [mdl '/Term'])

parameters.name: EventType (Event Listener)
parameters.description: 'Terminate'.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Terminate Function', [mdl '/Term']);
set_param([mdl '/Term/State Reader'], 'StateOwnerBlock', [mdl '/Integrator']);
tools.notes: Generates a terminate entry point in component code; pair with Initialize Function to persist and restore states across power cycles.

tools.name: Event Listener
tools.description: The event port inside Initialize, Reinitialize, Reset and Terminate Function blocks. It defines which model event executes the containing subsystem and, for reinitialize/reset, the event name.
tools.usage: Found inside Initialize/Reinitialize/Reset/Terminate Function subsystems; set_param([subsys '/Event Listener'], 'EventType', ...)

parameters.name: EventType
parameters.description: 'Initialize' (default), 'Reinitialize', 'Reset' or 'Terminate'.

parameters.name: EventName
parameters.description: Event name for reinitialize/reset events, e.g. 'reinit' or 'reset'.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: 'on' enables a variant condition so the event subsystem can be conditionally included.

tools.example: set_param([mdl '/Init/Event Listener'], 'EventType', 'Reinitialize', 'EventName', 'reinit');
tools.notes: Changing EventType effectively converts the subsystem between the four event-function flavours.

tools.name: State Reader
tools.description: Reads the state of a state-owner block (Integrator, Unit Delay, Discrete-Time Integrator, Delay, Stateflow chart and others) without a signal line. Typically used inside Terminate or Reset Function blocks to capture a state value.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > State Reader  |  select a state-owner block, then toolstrip Block tab > Reader-Writer > State Reader Block

parameters.name: StateOwnerBlock
parameters.description: Path of the block whose state is read (default '').

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/State Reader', [mdl '/Term/Read']);
set_param([mdl '/Term/Read'], 'StateOwnerBlock', [mdl '/Integrator']);
tools.notes: The owner block shows a badge linking to its readers and writers. Readers and writers must be in the same model (not across a Model block boundary).

tools.name: State Writer
tools.description: Writes a new value into the state of a state-owner block, replacing the value the owner would compute. Used inside Initialize, Reinitialize and Reset Function blocks to set initial conditions from computed or loaded data.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > State Writer

parameters.name: StateOwnerBlock
parameters.description: Path of the block whose state is written.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/State Writer', [mdl '/Init/Write']);
set_param([mdl '/Init/Write'], 'StateOwnerBlock', [mdl '/Discrete-Time Integrator']);
tools.notes: The state owner's own initial condition is overridden when a writer executes during initialization.

tools.name: Parameter Writer
tools.description: Writes a value to a tunable block parameter, a model workspace variable or a base workspace/data dictionary variable in response to an event. Use it inside Initialize, Reinitialize or Reset Function blocks, or in a referenced model to update a model argument.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Parameter Writer

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: 'Block parameter', 'Model workspace variable' or 'Base workspace or data dictionary variable'.

parameters.name: ParameterOwnerBlock / ParameterName
parameters.description: Block and parameter to write when Destination is a block parameter.

parameters.name: WorkspaceVariableName
parameters.description: Variable name when writing to a workspace.

parameters.name: IsParameterValidationOn
parameters.description: Validate that written values respect the parameter's range.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Parameter Writer', [mdl '/Init/PW']);
set_param([mdl '/Init/PW'], 'Destination', 'Model workspace variable', 'WorkspaceVariableName', 'Kp');
tools.notes: The target parameter must be tunable (not inlined by DefaultParameterBehavior).

tools.name: Message Triggered Subsystem
tools.description: Subsystem whose execution is controlled by an incoming message: it runs once per message arriving at its trigger port and the message payload is available inside. In immediate mode it executes as soon as the message is sent; in scheduled mode it runs in the Schedule Editor order.
tools.usage: Simulink > Ports & Subsystems > Message Triggered Subsystem  |  add_block('simulink/Ports & Subsystems/Message Triggered Subsystem', [mdl '/OnMsg'])

parameters.name: TriggerType (Trigger block)
parameters.description: 'message'.

parameters.name: ScheduleAsAperiodicPartition (Trigger block)
parameters.description: 'on' runs the subsystem in scheduled mode as an aperiodic partition; 'off' gives immediate mode.

tools.notes: Can be connected directly to a Send block or behind a Queue. Used heavily for event-driven software architectures.

tools.name: Variant Sink
tools.description: Routes one input signal to one of several outputs, with only the output whose variant condition is true active; blocks connected to inactive outputs are removed from simulation or code. It is the destination-side counterpart of Variant Source.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Variant Sink  |  add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Variant Sink', [mdl '/VSink'])

parameters.name: VariantControlMode
parameters.description: 'expression', 'label' or 'sim codegen switching'.

parameters.name: VariantControls
parameters.description: Cell array of conditions, one per output, e.g. {'V==1','V==2'}; '(default)' is allowed.

parameters.name: VariantActivationTime
parameters.description: 'update diagram', 'update diagram analyze all choices', 'code compile', 'startup' or 'inherit from Simulink.VariantControl'.

parameters.name: AllowZeroVariantControls
parameters.description: 'on' allows no output to be active.

parameters.name: ShowConditionOnBlock
parameters.description: 'on' displays the conditions on the block icon.

tools.notes: 'code compile' keeps all choices in generated code guarded by #if preprocessor conditionals; 'startup' allows switching at model startup without regeneration.

tools.name: Manual Variant Source
tools.description: Toggle-switch style variant block: double-clicking it cycles which of its input choices is passed to the output, and the inactive choices are removed from the compiled model. Handy for quick manual experiments without defining variant control variables.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Manual Variant Source

parameters.name: NumChoices
parameters.description: Number of variant input ports (default '2', minimum 2); set through the mask.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Manual Variant Source', [mdl '/Pick']);
set_param([mdl '/Pick'], 'NumChoices', '3');
tools.notes: Choice selection is a GUI action; for scripted or code-generated variant selection use Variant Source with variant control variables.

tools.name: Manual Variant Sink
tools.description: Toggle-switch variant block that passes its single input to one of several outputs, selected by double-clicking the block. Downstream blocks on inactive outputs are excluded from the compiled model.
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Manual Variant Sink

parameters.name: NumChoices
parameters.description: Number of variant output ports (minimum 2).

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Manual Variant Sink', [mdl '/Route']);
set_param([mdl '/Route'], 'NumChoices', '2');
tools.notes: Use Variant Sink for condition-driven selection.

tools.name: Index Vector
tools.description: A preconfigured Multiport Switch with one data port and zero-based indexing: the control input selects which element of the data vector is passed to the output. It is the block equivalent of y = u(idx+1).
tools.usage: Simulink > Signal Routing > Index Vector  |  add_block('simulink/Signal Routing/Index Vector', [mdl '/Idx'])

parameters.name: DataPortOrder
parameters.description: 'Zero-based contiguous' (default), 'One-based contiguous' or 'Specify indices'.

parameters.name: Inputs
parameters.description: Number of data ports (default '1').

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, default 'Inherit: Inherit via internal rule'.

parameters.name: RndMeth / SaturateOnIntegerOverflow
parameters.description: Integer rounding and overflow handling.

tools.notes: Its BlockType is MultiportSwitch, so find_system with BlockType 'MultiportSwitch' also returns Index Vector blocks.

tools.name: Interpreted MATLAB Function
tools.description: Applies a MATLAB function or expression to its input by calling the MATLAB interpreter at every evaluation. It lets you use any MATLAB function quickly, but is slow and does not support code generation.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > Interpreted MATLAB Function

parameters.name: MATLABFcn
parameters.description: Function name or expression using u, e.g. 'myfun(u)' or 'sin(u(1))*u(2)'.

parameters.name: OutputDimensions
parameters.description: Output dimensions; -1 means same as input.

parameters.name: OutputSignalType
parameters.description: 'auto', 'real' or 'complex'.

parameters.name: CollapseTo1D
parameters.description: 'on' collapses 2-D results to 1-D.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time, default -1 (inherited).

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/Interpreted MATLAB Function', [mdl '/F']);
set_param([mdl '/F'], 'MATLABFcn', 'norm(u)', 'OutputDimensions', '1');
tools.notes: Deprecated in recent releases: prefer the MATLAB Function block (compiled, code-generation capable) or Fcn for simple expressions.

tools.name: Fcn
tools.description: Applies a scalar C-style mathematical expression to its input vector u, e.g. 'sin(u(1))*exp(-u(2))'. It supports arithmetic, relational and logical operators and common math functions and generates efficient inline code.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > Fcn  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/Fcn', [mdl '/Expr'])

parameters.name: Expr
parameters.description: Expression in terms of u (u(1), u(2), ...) and workspace variables; output is scalar.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time, default -1.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/Fcn', [mdl '/Expr']);
set_param([mdl '/Expr'], 'Expr', 'K*u(1)^2 + u(2)');
tools.notes: The expression is not tunable during simulation or in generated code. Restored to the User-Defined Functions library in R2023a; for vector outputs use MATLAB Function.

tools.name: S-Function
tools.description: Hosts a compiled C, C++ or Fortran MEX S-function (or a Level-1 MATLAB S-function) that implements custom block behaviour through the S-function callback methods (mdlInitializeSizes, mdlOutputs, mdlUpdate, ...). It is the lowest-level extension mechanism and supports code generation through inlined TLC files.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > S-Function  |  add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/S-Function', [mdl '/SF'])

parameters.name: FunctionName
parameters.description: Name of the S-function MEX file without extension (default 'system').

parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of MATLAB expressions passed to the S-function, e.g. 'A, B, [1 2]'.

parameters.name: SFunctionModules
parameters.description: Additional source files needed to build the S-function for code generation.

tools.notes: Build MEX files with mex and a supported compiler. The Legacy Code Tool and S-Function Builder can generate S-functions automatically; C Caller and C Function are simpler for plain C code.

tools.name: S-Function Builder
tools.description: Generates a C MEX S-function (plus optional TLC file) from C code you enter in a graphical editor: ports, parameters, states and the outputs/update/derivatives code sections. Pressing Build creates and compiles the S-function so the block becomes a working custom block.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > S-Function Builder  |  double-click, fill in ports and code sections, click Build

parameters.name: S-function name
parameters.description: Name of the generated S-function source/MEX file.

parameters.name: Ports and Parameters table
parameters.description: Input/output ports, dimensions, data types and block parameters.

parameters.name: Build options
parameters.description: Generate wrapper TLC for code generation, enable debugging, add libraries/includes.

tools.notes: Requires a supported C compiler (mex -setup C). The builder regenerates source on every build, so keep custom code in the editor rather than editing generated files.

tools.name: Level-2 MATLAB S-Function
tools.description: Runs a Level-2 MATLAB S-function: a MATLAB file whose setup function registers callback methods (Outputs, Update, Derivatives, ...) through the run-time block object. It provides full S-function flexibility without compiling C.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > Level-2 MATLAB S-Function

parameters.name: FunctionName
parameters.description: Name of the MATLAB S-function file (default 'matlabfile').

parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.description: Comma-separated parameter expressions in the order the S-function expects.

tools.notes: Runs in interpreted MATLAB, so it is slower than C MEX. Code generation requires a hand-written inlining TLC file.

tools.name: C Function
tools.description: Embeds C/C++ statements directly in the block for output, start, initialize-conditions and terminate phases, with a symbol table mapping ports, parameters and persistent data to C variables. It integrates small pieces of legacy code or C++ objects without writing an S-function.
tools.usage: Simulink > User-Defined Functions > C Function

parameters.name: OutputCode / StartCode / InitializeConditionsCode / TerminateCode
parameters.description: C code executed in each phase during simulation; Codegen-prefixed versions apply to generated code.

parameters.name: SymbolSpec
parameters.description: Ports and Parameters table: symbol names, scope (Input, Output, Parameter, Persistent, Constant), type and size.

parameters.name: CustomCodeSettingLocation
parameters.description: 'BlockSettings', 'ModelConfigurationParameters' or 'UpdateBuildInfo' - where headers, sources and libraries are specified.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Block sample time, default -1.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/User-Defined Functions/C Function', [mdl '/CF']);
set_param([mdl '/CF'], 'OutputCode', 'y = saturate(u, lo, hi);', 'SimCustomHeaderFile', '#include "sat.h"');
tools.notes: Compared with C Caller, C Function allows arbitrary statements and persistent state instead of calling a single existing function.

tools.name: Assertion
tools.description: Checks at every time step that all elements of its input are nonzero; if any element is zero it stops the simulation with an error (default) or issues a warning and optionally runs a callback. Drive it with a Relational Operator or logic to express run-time requirements.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Assertion  |  add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Assertion', [mdl '/Assert'])

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: 'on' | 'off' - enable the check.

parameters.name: AssertionFailFcn
parameters.description: MATLAB expression executed when the assertion fails.

parameters.name: stopWhenAssertionFail
parameters.description: 'on' stops the simulation with an error; 'off' only warns.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time, default -1.

tools.notes: All Model Verification blocks are globally controlled by the AssertControl model parameter ('UseLocalSettings', 'EnableAll', 'DisableAll'). Assertions are ignored in generated code unless the target supports them.

tools.name: Check Static Range
tools.description: Asserts that the input signal stays within a fixed range [min, max] at every time step, with each bound selectable as inclusive or exclusive. Use it to catch out-of-range sensor values or actuator commands during simulation.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Static Range

parameters.name: max / max_included
parameters.description: Upper bound (default '100') and whether it is inclusive.

parameters.name: min / min_included
parameters.description: Lower bound (default '0') and whether it is inclusive.

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail
parameters.description: Enable the check and stop on failure.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: MATLAB expression run on failure.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the Boolean assertion result as a signal.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Static Range', [mdl '/Range']);
set_param([mdl '/Range'], 'min', '-10', 'max', '10', 'stopWhenAssertionFail', 'off', 'export', 'on');
tools.notes: Implemented as a masked Assertion; Simulink Design Verifier can use the same blocks as proof objectives.

tools.name: Check Dynamic Range
tools.description: Asserts that a test signal lies between two other signals (min and max inputs) at each time step. Use it when the allowed envelope itself varies over time, such as a tolerance band around a reference trajectory.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Dynamic Range (inputs: min, sig, max)

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail
parameters.description: Enable the check and stop on failure.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: MATLAB expression executed on failure.

parameters.name: export
parameters.description: 'on' outputs the assertion result.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Dynamic Range', [mdl '/Band']);
add_line(mdl, 'RefLo/1', 'Band/1'); add_line(mdl, 'y/1', 'Band/2'); add_line(mdl, 'RefHi/1', 'Band/3');
tools.notes: The three inputs are the lower bound (min), the test signal (sig) and the upper bound (max); bounds may be scalars or match the signal dimensions.

tools.name: Check Static Lower Bound
tools.description: Asserts that the input is greater than (or equal to) a constant lower bound at every step. A one-sided version of Check Static Range.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Static Lower Bound

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Lower bound value.

parameters.name: min_included
parameters.description: 'on' makes the bound inclusive (>=).

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Static Lower Bound', [mdl '/Pmin']);
set_param([mdl '/Pmin'], 'min', '0', 'min_included', 'off');
tools.notes: Use Check Dynamic Lower Bound when the bound is a signal.

tools.name: Check Static Upper Bound
tools.description: Asserts that the input is less than (or equal to) a constant upper bound at every step. Typical use: verifying temperatures, currents or speeds never exceed a limit.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Static Upper Bound

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Upper bound value.

parameters.name: max_included
parameters.description: 'on' makes the bound inclusive (<=).

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Static Upper Bound', [mdl '/Tmax']);
set_param([mdl '/Tmax'], 'max', '120');
tools.notes: Failures are reported in the Diagnostic Viewer with the block path and time.

tools.name: Check Dynamic Lower Bound
tools.description: Asserts that a test signal is always greater than a second, time-varying bound signal. Inputs are the bound (min) and the test signal (sig).
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Dynamic Lower Bound (inputs: min, sig)

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example: add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Dynamic Lower Bound', [mdl '/AboveRef']);
tools.notes: Both inputs must have the same dimensions or the bound must be scalar.

tools.name: Check Dynamic Upper Bound
tools.description: Asserts that a test signal is always less than a second, time-varying bound signal. Inputs are the bound (max) and the test signal (sig).
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Dynamic Upper Bound (inputs: max, sig)

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example: add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Dynamic Upper Bound', [mdl '/BelowLimit']);
tools.notes: Useful for checking a signal against a speed- or temperature-dependent limit computed elsewhere in the model.

tools.name: Check Static Gap
tools.description: Asserts that the input stays outside a fixed forbidden interval (a gap) between a lower and an upper bound. Use it for dead bands or resonance regions a signal must never dwell in.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Static Gap

parameters.name: max / max_included
parameters.description: Upper edge of the gap and inclusivity.

parameters.name: min / min_included
parameters.description: Lower edge of the gap and inclusivity.

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Static Gap', [mdl '/NotInBand']);
set_param([mdl '/NotInBand'], 'min', '1450', 'max', '1550');
tools.notes: The signal passes if it is <= min or >= max (depending on inclusivity).

tools.name: Check Dynamic Gap
tools.description: Asserts that a signal stays outside a gap whose edges are given by two other time-varying signals. The gap edges are supplied as two extra input signals.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Dynamic Gap (three inputs: the test signal and the gap's lower and upper edges, as labelled on the block)

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export / icon
parameters.description: Common assertion options and icon style ('graphic' or 'text').

tools.example: add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Dynamic Gap', [mdl '/Gap']);
tools.notes: Ensure the min input is actually below the max input; otherwise every value passes or fails unexpectedly.

tools.name: Check Discrete Gradient
tools.description: Asserts that the absolute difference between successive samples of a discrete signal is below a maximum gradient. Use it to detect jumps, glitches or slew-rate violations.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Discrete Gradient

parameters.name: gradient
parameters.description: Maximum allowed |u(k) - u(k-1)| (default '1').

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Discrete Gradient', [mdl '/Slew']);
set_param([mdl '/Slew'], 'gradient', '0.5');
tools.notes: Requires a fixed-step discrete solver (discrete signal).

tools.name: Check Input Resolution
tools.description: Asserts that the input signal has a specified resolution, i.e. is an integer multiple of a scalar resolution or matches one of a vector of allowed values. Useful for verifying quantised signals such as ADC outputs.
tools.usage: Simulink > Model Verification > Check Input Resolution

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Scalar step size or vector of permitted values (default '1').

parameters.name: enabled / stopWhenAssertionFail / callback / export
parameters.description: Common assertion options.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Model Verification/Check Input Resolution', [mdl '/Quant']);
set_param([mdl '/Quant'], 'resolution', '2^-10');
tools.notes: Floating-point round-off can cause false failures with non-power-of-two resolutions.
